headline: Congress cancels a Department of Energy rule that set stricter energy-efficiency standards for commercial refrigerators and freezers.
what_it_does: This law uses the Congressional Review Act to cancel a Department of Energy rule published on January 21, 2025. That rule set new, stricter energy-efficiency standards for commercial refrigerators, freezers, and refrigerator-freezers, with a compliance deadline of January 22, 2029. Because the rule is cancelled, this equipment no longer has to meet those new standards.

who_it_affects.group: Makers of commercial refrigerators and freezers
who_it_affects.how: They no longer have to redesign equipment to meet the stricter standards by January 22, 2029.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses that buy commercial refrigeration equipment, such as grocery stores, restaurants, and convenience stores
who_it_affects.how: The equipment they buy will not be required to meet the new, higher efficiency levels set by the cancelled rule.
The department's Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy cannot enforce the cancelled rule.

when_it_takes_effect: May 9, 2025, when the law was enacted; the cancelled rule's January 22, 2029 compliance deadline no longer applies.
